subject.title: fix: persist pending followup queues across gateway restart

question: Should maintainers continue this stale JSON-sidecar PR as the restart-recovery implementation path, or route the canonical issue to a SQLite-backed successor such as the newer open candidate?
rationale: The remaining blockers are architecture and trust-boundary choices across durable state, replay semantics, and overlapping open PRs, not a narrow mechanical patch that automation can safely choose.

options.title: Rebuild as SQLite-backed recovery
options.body: Move durable followup queue state into shared SQLite with doctor/migration handling, preserve the current startup surface, and prove upgrade plus exactly-once replay before merge.

options.title: Focus the newer SQLite candidate
options.body: Use this PR as context and continue review on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82572 only if it becomes clean, proof-positive, and free of blocking findings.

options.title: Approve the sidecar deliberately
options.body: Maintainers could explicitly own the JSON sidecar, trusted replay, stale-drop, and duplicate-replay risks, but that should be an intentional product and architecture decision.

recommendation.title: Rebuild as SQLite-backed recovery
recommendation.body: Move durable followup queue state into shared SQLite with doctor/migration handling, preserve the current startup surface, and prove upgrade plus exactly-once replay before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest recent history across the queue and gateway lifecycle surface and can route the architecture choice to the right owner boundary.
